value.rationale: Binary16 is a standard finite precision used in numerical dynamics, and complete cycle periods and basin sizes determine the actual recurrence and data diversity of deterministic digital trajectories. The newly classified one-round semantics collapses the natural nonzero recurrent period from 40 to 5 and its nonzero-cycle basin from 10,267 to 117, while redirecting 15,236 states to zero, despite only 2,774 changed local transition edges. This exact, full-state distinction is scientifically relevant to reproducibility and forecast-error diagnostics for chaotic-map arithmetic, rather than an arbitrarily chosen bit subset. The known qualitative order-dependence and staged 40-cycle are credited to earlier work; numerical verification and novelty alone are not the rationale for value.
